findings.title: Light and dark lightness values are swapped, so the light theme changes from 30% to 70%.
findings.body: The old rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light branch uses 70%, so poster names in `.topic-meta-data h5 a` become much paler on light themes. Every other replacement in this PR keeps the original light value and uses 100−X for the dark branch. The fix is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: The light-theme color for `.group-member-info .name` changes from 30% to 50%.
findings.body: The old rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new light branch uses 50%. That changes the light theme, which this PR is not meant to touch. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: The values for `.custom-message-length` are inverted, so the hint becomes much darker on light themes.
findings.body: The old rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a pale hint. The new light branch uses 30% and the dark branch uses 70%, which inverts the intent on both themes. The desktop version of this rule correctly uses (70%, 30%). Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: The light-theme color for the topic map `h3` on mobile changes from 20% to 50%.
findings.body: The old rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the new light branch uses 50%, so the heading gets lighter on light themes. The desktop version of this rule uses (20%, 80%). Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: The light-theme color for `.group-member-info .name` on mobile changes from 30% to 50%.
findings.body: This is the same mistake as in the desktop file. The original light-theme lightness was 30%, and the new light branch uses 50%, so the light theme renders differently. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.
